On 2026-08-31 sid superseded the per-PR michael trio (/think-like-michael, /review-like-michael, /save-from-myself) because /pre-pr-review covers what they caught. The trio's command files still exist in ~/.claude/commands but are no longer part of the standing workflow; only invoke them if sid explicitly asks.

**Why:** the trio and /pre-pr-review overlapped heavily (all simulate the human review), and the team's new PR template (ENG-2206) added its own gates (scope-check section, delegated-review checkbox — satisfied by /pre-pr-review as the "other full-review workflow").

**How to apply, in order per PR:**
1. During implementation: `roam-global-tailwind` when touching Roam UI styling.
2. After push: `/pre-pr-review` as an independent Opus pass (see [[feedback_independent_pre_pr_review]]); rerun after follow-up pushes.
3. PR assembly: `scope-check` against the ticket's Done When; paste its `## Scope check` section into the PR body, which starts from `.github/pull_request_template.md` (see [[feedback-no-claude-footer-simple-prs]]).

5. All team-facing prose uses `dg-engineering-writing-style`; tickets use `dg-create-engineering-ticket` (see [[feedback-use-dg-ticket-skills]]).

=== feedback_worktree_node_modules_symlink.md
---
name: feedback_worktree_node_modules_symlink
description: Worktree node_modules — symlink from main repo ONLY if the branch doesn't touch packages/*; otherwise full `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in the worktree
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: b71984ac-c6a8-436b-8762-7148435b6578
  modified: 2026-09-25T12:11:45.600Z
---

Git worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/` start with **no `node_modules`** — checks fail with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: @repo/eslint-config` because this is a pnpm workspace and `@repo/*` packages live in per-package `node_modules`.

**Why (updated 2026-07-10, ENG-2019):** Symlinks resolve `@repo/*` workspace packages to the MAIN repo's checkout. That's only correct when the worktree branch leaves `packages/*` untouched. If the branch adds/changes anything in `packages/*`, tsc/eslint see the stale main-repo copy; and MIXED states (some dirs symlinked, some real from a filtered install) are worst of all — one mix broke Roam's global types, another broke Obsidian's React 18/19 peer resolution.

**How to apply:**
- Branch touches only `apps/*` code: symlink root + per-package `node_modules` from the main repo (fast, gitignored, never committed).
- Branch touches `packages/*`: run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` at the worktree root instead (shared pnpm store, ~5–45s). If a mixed symlink/real state exists, remove the symlinks and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --force` to rebuild the virtual store cleanly.
- Never run `--no-frozen-lockfile` casually: it re-resolves unrelated packages (an @types/node dedup cascaded into React type mixing that broke Obsidian tsc, would have been red CI). To add one dep, hand-add the importer entry to pnpm-lock.yaml reusing an existing catalog resolution (PR #1216 did it in 3 lines), then frozen install.

**Root `pnpm ci:validate` in a symlinked worktree (2026-09-02, ENG-2141):** symlink EVERY workspace that has a package.json, not just the ones you touch. `apps/tldraw-sync-worker/node_modules` was missing and turbo failed fast on its `check-types`, skipping every other task. Separately, the main checkout's virtual-store hoist `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/@types/react` was a July link to React 18 types while packages/ui needs 19, so `@repo/ui check-types` failed locally even though `.pnpm/lock.yaml` matched the lockfile and CI at the same commit was green. That is a main-checkout environment problem (a fresh frozen install there), not something to fix from a worktree. Fallback proof when it bites: `pnpm exec turbo run test:unit` at the worktree root plus per-app `tsc`, and cite the green CI run at the base SHA.

**Husky rewrites the shared hooks path (2026-09-25):** `pnpm install` in a worktree runs the root `prepare` script (`husky`), which sets the repo-wide `core.hooksPath` to relative `.husky/_`. The main checkout's value is absolute `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.husky/_` (the Entire hook wrappers live there). After any worktree install, check `git config core.hooksPath` and restore the absolute value if it changed.

See [[feedback_stay_in_worktree]], [[feedback_rename_worktree_branch_before_push]], [[feedback_fix_relocated_lint_warnings]].

=== feedback_stay_in_worktree.md
---
name: feedback-stay-in-worktree
description: "When the session env says the working dir is a git worktree, never cd to the main repo path — Bash cwd persists, and absolute Edit paths will silently target the wrong checkout"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 66a59f46-b22d-467a-93d6-1726749382d8
  modified: 2026-08-10T15:01:23.000Z
---

When the session environment header says `Primary working directory: /mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/<TICKET>`, do not `cd` out of that worktree for ANY command — not for lint, not for tsc, not for grep, not for anything.

**Why:** The Bash tool's cwd persists between commands. The moment I run `cd /mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/apps/roam && npx eslint ...`, every subsequent `Edit` with an absolute path under `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/apps/roam/...` lands in the main repo on `main`, not the worktree. The Edit tool happily writes the file because the path exists — there is no warning. By the time I notice (often only when the user says "I don't see it in my IDE"), the main branch's working tree has half a PR's worth of uncommitted changes, and the worktree is empty.

This happened once on ENG-1660: 5 files edited in main on branch `main` instead of the worktree. Recovery required `git diff > patch`, `git apply` in worktree, `git restore` in main. Easy to fix but a real risk every time — if the user had run `git add -A && git commit` from main while I was still editing, my changes would land on `main` directly.

**Second failure mode (ENG-1575): a read-only `cd` poisons the build/copy/verify pipeline.** Here the Edits were fine (absolute worktree paths), but I `cd`'d to `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/apps/roam` for a *harmless-feeling* read-only peek at shared `node_modules` (Blueprint source) and never cd'd back. The next `npm run build`, `npx eslint/tsc`, and `cp dist/.` all inherited main as cwd — so I built `main` (none of the PR's commits), copied that to the test dir, and the "passing" lint/tsc validated main's unedited file. I shipped a wrong build to the user's test dir and reported it as correct. The read-only cd is the sneaky one: it doesn't trip the Edit-path check, so nothing feels wrong until the artifact is already out. **Detection cue:** print `pwd` + `git rev-parse --short HEAD` at the top of any build/check command — if HEAD isn't the worktree branch's tip, cwd has drifted.

**How to apply:**
- Use absolute paths starting with the worktree path: `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/<TICKET>/apps/roam/...`.
- For Bash commands that have a working-directory requirement (lint, prettier, tsc, pnpm scripts), use `git -C <worktree>` or run from the worktree path: `(cd /mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/<TICKET>/apps/roam && npx eslint ...)` so the subshell exits without changing the parent cwd.
- Or use `pushd`/`popd` style: `cd /path/to/worktree/apps/roam && ... && cd -`.
- Before any `Edit` call when working in a worktree session, double-check the path starts with the worktree path, not the main-repo path.
- If you must `cd` (e.g., for `npx` to find the right `package.json`), `cd` only to a subdirectory of the worktree.

metadata:

`refs/stash` is a single ref shared by ALL worktrees of a repository. During the 2026-07-05 six-agent parallel run, two subagents ran `git stash`/`git stash pop` concurrently in sibling worktrees: one popped the other's WIP into its tree and both stashes were ejected/dropped (recovered via dangling commits).

**Why:** stash push/pop in any worktree mutates the same stack; concurrent use is a race. Note the repo's husky/lint-staged pre-commit hook ALSO stashes (backup) on every commit, so even parallel `git commit`s across worktrees can race.

**How to apply:**
- Tell subagents working in parallel worktrees: never use `git stash`; diff against HEAD or copy files to the scratchpad instead.
- Run commits across worktrees sequentially, never in parallel (the pre-commit hook stashes).
- The stash stack holds ~6 old WIP entries from past sessions; don't pop them casually — ownership is unclear.

Related: [[feedback_merge_just_commit]] (never stash mid-merge), [[feedback_worktree_node_modules_symlink]].

**Heuristic (weighted, not applied everywhere):** when the pre-PR review (Codex, per [[feedback-pr-workflow-skills]]) surfaces a finding that is really a design fork ("is this gap inside Done When?", "would fixing it be scope creep?", "keep or change an inherited decision?"), run `scope-check` on the fork itself before taking the question to sid. It answers three things: which side of the `Done When` boundary each option lands on, whether the current diff already sits inside it, and whether deferring a fix needs a recorded decision. It does not pick the option and it does not decide coverage gaps; that stays with sid.

**Where the record lives (sid, 2026-09-23): on the PR, in the top-level "Decision:" comment, never on Linear.** The scope-check skill text says "a Linear comment before merge"; sid overrode that. On PR #1473 the inline notes cited "D2 on ENG-2293" while the trace sat unposted in a scratchpad (the API key was read-only), and maparent asked "Where are D2, D3 accessible?". Post the Decision comment before the inline notes reference it, and make every pointer (inline notes, review summary, PR body) name that comment. **Only the decisions the notes actually cite go in it**: when I expanded it to a D1 to D6 trace, sid's reaction was "this is now too much, just do the ones we are mentioning". Design rationale that no note cites stays in the PR body's reviewer brief or nowhere.

**When it carries weight:** the question is about the acceptance boundary or an inherited decision from a prior ticket. **When it carries none:** plain correctness bugs (fix them), questions the ticket text answers outright, pure mechanism or UX taste with no Done When angle. Do not run it on every finding or every task.

**Why:** 2026-09-21, ENG-2293. Codex flagged two P2s: the discovery list's 1,000-row cap leaves an accessible Source un-imported at scale, and re-import leaves an old placeholder title because the materializer's timestamp-only skip (decided on ENG-2142 / PR #1331) runs before title resolution. I took both to sid as open questions. Sid asked whether scope-check could answer them first. It settled the second (the fix would alter #1331's skip semantics shared with Refresh, so keeping is the in-scope choice) and framed the first (inside Done When 1 either way, so the list-only design needs a recorded deferral). One round-trip saved, and the residual decision reached sid already framed.

**How to apply:**
1. After the review pass, sort findings into bugs (fix), spec-answered (apply), and forks (run scope-check on the fork's options, not just the diff).
2. Take to sid only what remains, with the boundary classification attached and a recommendation.
3. **Whenever this heuristic was applied, say so explicitly at the end of the work message:** name the fork it was run on and what it settled. sid wants to see when it fired.

=================== PR_GUIDELINES.md
# PR guidelines

This is the repository source for the DevOps PR process. Code standards live in [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md); agent instructions live in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Production changes, releases, and work intake remain in DevOps.

## Scope and structure

- Use one PR per Linear ticket. You may batch very minor, unrelated changes of a few lines when they are low risk.
- Scope the ticket to one specific problem. If additional problems need attention, pause that additional work and check with the team or lead before implementing it.
- Use separate PRs for unrelated refactors, feature additions, dependency updates, and lint or style fixes. Keep scope to a single package or app when possible.
- For features spanning packages, make foundational changes such as types and shared utilities first, then use separate PRs for usage and integration.

## Size and review guidance

About 200 added plus removed lines is a useful target. Up to 400 lines is acceptable when the change is scoped and self-contained. Ideally, touch fewer than five files; repetitive mechanical changes can justify more. These are review guidelines, not automatic rejection thresholds.

Test changes do not count toward the 400-line threshold.

Above 400 changed lines, explain why the PR cannot reasonably be split. Include the main review entry points and intended testing path in Reviewer brief. Keep this concise rather than adding a file-by-file summary.

## Branches and PR metadata

- Use Linear's generated branch name through Copy Branch Name.
- For Linear-backed work, use `ENG-#### Exact Linear ticket title` as the PR title. This is the repository convention in place of the alternative title formats previously listed in DevOps.
- Start with [.github/pull_request_template.md](.github/pull_request_template.md). Treat the ticket as the source of truth rather than restating it. Follow the PR body guidance in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#pull-request-bodies).

## Before requesting review

- Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then `pnpm ci:validate` from the repository root before opening a PR or declaring it ready. Resolve failures before requesting review. A draft must disclose unresolved validation blockers.
- Check applicable build and lint commands. Manually exercise changed behavior end-to-end, including relevant edge cases and alternative flows. Verification is optional; use it when checks and results help the reviewer.
- Read the complete final diff and review it against [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md), including added and modified comments. Use inline PR comments for review-specific explanations and durable code comments for constraints future changes must preserve.
- Run `$scope-check` against the ENG ticket and final diff. Paste its Scope check section into the PR body. If `Done When` is missing, leave the checkbox unchecked and state that explicitly.
- Run `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata. Check the Standards check box when it has run. Make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them.
- Complete the Local delegated full review required by the template, using `$dg-delegated-full-review` when no other full-review workflow is available.
- Include a Loom video for every PR, including backend, refactor, and infrastructure changes. Keep it under 2–3 minutes, show before/after for bug fixes, and narrate key decisions. Put the link in Loom video.
- Assign a reviewer when ready. Do not mark a draft ready while required evidence or reviews remain incomplete.

## After merge

Delete the PR branch after a successful merge. Creating a draft does not authorize merging or deleting branches.

# PR adherence check

Review the final change against the repository's current rules. Remain read-only unless the user authorizes fixes or PR updates. Do not post comments, request reviews, or change ticket status as part of this check.

## Resolve the evidence

1. Use the supplied PR or resolve the current branch's PR. Read its title, base and head commits, complete diff, body, checks, and review state. Separately make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them; do not require these details in the PR body. # Scope Check

Compare the completed change with its acceptance boundary. Return a copy-ready `Scope check` section unless the user requests the analysis too.

## Gather the Inputs

1. Resolve the Linear issue from an explicit `ENG-###` identifier, then from the PR or branch name. Fetch the issue with the Linear connector. If it is unavailable, ask for the ticket's `Problem`, `Solution`, and `Done When` sections.
2. Treat `Done When` as the acceptance boundary. Use `Problem` and `Solution` only to clarify that boundary, not to silently expand it.
3. Resolve the final change set from the supplied diff or PR. For a PR, inspect its metadata and complete diff. For the current branch, compare it with the PR base branch and include staged and unstaged changes.
4. Read linked decisions or ticket comments only when they explain an apparent scope expansion.

## Evaluate Scope

Map every material behavior or architectural change to a `Done When` criterion.

- Treat implementation details, tests, documentation, and generated files required to satisfy `Done When` as in scope.
- Flag broader abstractions, unrelated refactors, new dependencies, migrations, or support for cases not required by `Done When`.
- Do not treat a change as in scope only because it is useful or adjacent.

For each scope expansion, determine:

1. What broader abstraction or additional case was introduced?
2. Which current use case or ticket requires it, and why must it be included now rather than deferred?
3. Was anyone affected or consulted, and where is the discussion or decision recorded?

Do not invent missing justification. Mark it `Not documented` and recommend recording it in a Linear comment before the PR is merged.

## Format the Result

Use this form when the diff stays within scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: None.
```

Use this form when the diff expands scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: <what changed>
- Required now: <use case or ticket and why it cannot be deferred>
- Anyone affected or consulted: <Yes, No, or Not documented>
- Decision: <link to the discussion or decision, or `Not documented`>
```

If the ticket or diff cannot be resolved, leave the checkbox unchecked and state exactly what input is missing. Keep findings short and evidence-based.

Do not modify the issue, PR, or implementation unless the user explicitly asks.

<skill-prompt>
Run a pre-PR review of the current change set. This is NOT a checklist to ponder — it is a sequence of verification steps with pass/fail outcomes. You must actually run the greps/traces; "I believe this is fine" without having looked is a failed step. Built from an autopsy of 97 real reviewer comments (2026-03→07) — 46 violated rules a previous skill already "had" but never enforced; recall is not verification — and refreshed 2026-08-28 against the 2026-07→08 corpus (~200 human review comments across sid's and teammates' PRs).

Required reading before step 1 (both live in `<repo-root>/.claude/context/`, repo root `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph` — reachable by absolute path from any worktree):
- `engineering-context.md` — team philosophies and hard-learned lessons (the *why* behind every check below)
- `db-domain-invariants.md` — current schema/data-layer facts (the data-layer pass checks the diff against every entry)

## Mode gate (run FIRST, before Step 0)

Decide which mode this run needs. This is a judgment call you make from evidence — not a rule to apply mechanically, and not something to take on faith from the dispatching prompt (dispatch prompts are written fresh each run and can get this wrong in either direction):
- Evidence a full pass already ran on this PR: a previous run's line-anchored annotations posted on the PR, existing review threads answering a prior findings report, or the dispatcher naming a last-reviewed SHA.
- Default when a full pass ran and the commits since only answer review feedback: Re-review mode below.
- A full pass on a follow-up push can still be the right call when there's genuine reason — the delta added surface beyond the feedback (the escape hatch below), the base moved under the branch, prior coverage looks doubtful or stale, or enough rounds have accumulated that the whole PR deserves fresh eyes. If you judge that, run full and say why.
- The first line of your output states the chosen mode and the reasoning — that's what keeps the choice reviewable, whichever way it goes.

## Step 0 — Inventory

The change set is the FULL PR diff: `git diff <base>...HEAD` (merge-base three-dot against the PR's base branch — the stack parent for stacked PRs, else main) plus staged/unstaged changes. Never review only the latest commits: reviewers see the whole PR, and code that landed on the branch before this run is still your surface. (Exception: Re-review mode below.) Classify changed files:
- **DATA**: `packages/database/**`, `*.sql`, any file containing a Supabase/PostgREST call (`.from(`), datalog query, or cross-app contract type
- **FRONTEND**: `apps/roam/**`, `apps/obsidian/**`, `apps/website/**` UI code
- **OTHER**: tests, docs, config

Steps 2 and 3 are scoped: skip the data-layer pass if no DATA files changed; skip the frontend pass if no FRONTEND files changed. Never skip steps 1 and 4.

## Re-review mode (follow-up pushes)

If a full pre-pr-review already ran on this PR and this run covers a follow-up push (fixes after a review round or a previous run's findings), do NOT repeat the full sequence:

- Change set = `git diff <last-reviewed-sha>...HEAD` — the commits since the state the previous round covered, not the whole PR again.
- **Findings closure first.** For every finding from the previous run and every reviewer/bot comment since: re-run the SPECIFIC check that produced it and report fixed / not-fixed / deferred+ticket per item. A fix claimed without re-verification is a failed step; a UI fix additionally gets re-driven (existing rule).
- Run steps 1–3 mechanically on the delta only, with Step 0's DATA/FRONTEND scoping applied to the delta. Step 4 shrinks to: every new hunk maps to the review feedback or the ticket, and the bot-comment gate on comments the new push attracted.
- Skip re-reading the context docs unless the delta touches DATA/FRONTEND files and they aren't already in context.
- Escape hatch: if the "follow-up" adds new surface (rebase onto a moved base, new feature code, a refactor beyond what was asked), it is not a re-review — run the full sequence on the full PR diff.

## Step 1 — Mechanical sweeps (always run; each is an action, not a question)

1a. **Reuse gate.** List every NEW named thing in the diff (function, type, component, constant, enum, marker string). For each, run a grep across `apps/roam/src/utils`, `packages/utils`, `packages/database/src`, and sibling files for the core operation or shape. Report what you searched and what you found. A new thing duplicating an existing one is a finding. Special case: every inline string-literal union (`"X" | "Y"`) gets its members grepped in `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts`; members matching a generated enum → must use `Enums<"…">`.

1b. **Justification sweep.** For every added default value, optional prop/field, state variable, fallback (`?? x`, `|| x`), and kept-through-refactor line: name the concrete code path that exercises it. Trace return types through call sites — if a function always returns `T`, a `?? fallback` at its call site is dead code; say so. No path → finding: delete it.

1c. **Literal hoist.** Repeated or typo-prone string literals (prop keys, selectors, attribute names, ids) appearing more than once or shared with other files → must be a named constant defined once.

1d. **Type honesty.** For every `as`, `any`, `unknown`, `!` (non-null assertion), `?.`, `void`, and `|| default` in the diff: can the value actually be null/absent there? Verify against the type at its source, don't guess. Assertion where a guard or upstream fix is possible → finding. A `!` that must survive gets an inline comment saying why it's safe — mdroidian flags every bare `!` (#1329, #1324).

1e. **Explainability.** For each hunk: one sentence, why is this here in service of the ticket? Reorderings, reformats, removals, and leftover scaffolding you can't explain → finding: revert.

1f. **Call-graph pass (review the resulting system, not the diff).** For every exported symbol added or modified, and every function parameter added: grep ALL call sites across `apps/` and `packages/` and read them. Findings:
- a parameter that only one caller supplies (or that every caller could omit) → internalize or remove it
- a wrapper that after this change only renames/forwards or adds one trivial field → collapse it into its caller
- an export with zero external consumers → unexport
- an existing caller whose behavior silently changes (check what it did with the old return shape — e.g. did it append `Z` to a timestamp you now normalize?)
Reviewers read the post-state code, not the diff; a hunk that looks justified in isolation can leave the system with dead indirection.

1g. **Comment audit.** List every comment line ADDED by the diff. Delete any that restates the code or narrates the change — "Claude, chill on the comments" is a real review quote, left twice (#1222, #1321), and "some unnecessary comments here" a third time (#1292). A comment referencing context not present in the file (another PR, a discussion, another platform's behavior) either becomes self-contained or dies: reviewers reply "What is F12?" / "What is the same reason?" to comments they can't parse cold (#1315, #1292, #1284). Keep only comments stating a constraint the code can't show.

1h. **Second-lookup check.** For every new fetch, map-build, `.find`, or helper lookup: trace where its input data was constructed — was the looked-up value already present there (on the row, the batch, an upstream type)? If yes → thread the field through the pipeline types instead of re-deriving downstream. (#1266: importer re-fetched `schema_id` that `SharedNode` already carried; #1317: `getFormatByNodeTypeUid()` second lookup when `matchingNodeType.format` was in hand at the construction site.)

1i. **Workflow injection (only if `.github/workflows/` changed).** Any `${{ inputs.* }}` / `${{ github.event.* }}` interpolated directly into a `run:` script is shell injection — pass it through `env:` and use a quoted variable, validated against a fully anchored pattern (#1253).

## Step 2 — Data-layer pass (only if DATA files changed)

2a. Open `db-domain-invariants.md` and check the diff against EVERY entry. For each entry state: applies / doesn't apply / VIOLATION. Do not summarize the file — walk it.

2b. **Provenance trace.** For every value read from a PostgREST response or datalog result used in the diff: name the source column, grep its type in `packages/database/supabase/schemas/*.sql`, then judge the code handling it (timestamps are the known killer — naive UTC, no `Z`).

2c. **Query review.** For every `.from(...)` chain (new or modified): required domain filters present (arity, is_schema, variant)? Any client-side `.filter`/`.find`/sort the request could express? Payload columns in a listing path? Paginated with a unique total order? Inside a loop that should be batched?

2d. **Contract check.** New/changed shared types: required-vs-optional modeled from real cases (does every producer actually supply it)? Identity carried once (RID) not duplicated decomposed? Consistent with `crossAppContracts.ts` and with what the Obsidian side already assumes — check its consumer code, don't assume.

2e. **Converter matrix.** A field added or renamed on a cross-app contract or schema type must be handled in EVERY converter, BOTH directions, or explicitly deferred with a ticket named in the PR. Enumerate the cells and mark each handled/deferred: `packages/database/src/lib/crossAppConverters.ts` (CrossApp→db), `packages/database/src/lib/dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` (db→CrossApp), `apps/roam/src/utils/roamToCrossAppConverters.ts`, and Obsidian's parse/produce paths (`importNodes.ts` parsers, publish side). maparent asked for the missing direction on #1316 AND #1317: "This PR is adding a field; it should handle that field in both translation directions."

2f. **Flag-gated writes.** For every new DB write path: which user-visible flag or action authorizes it? Sync flag off ⇒ the user expects NO DB communication; a silent maintenance write (backfill, migration) needs explicit call-out in the PR, and its outcome reports to PostHog — never a user toast (#1332).

## Step 3 — Frontend pass (only if FRONTEND files changed)

Check against the frontend lessons in `engineering-context.md`, mechanically:
- grep the diff for `style=`, `class-[`/`-[` arbitrary values, hex colors → Tailwind-scale violations
- grep for `window.roamAlphaAPI` legacy paths (sync `.q`, `async.backend`) → current-API violations
- settings writes → must go through block-props accessors, preserving the store gate
- new UI elements → which flag gates them (including EXISTING flags the new surface must respect, e.g. `autoCanvasRelations` on #1272); user-facing failures → PostHog + toast, not `console.error`
- names: every new variable/setter/label states exactly what it holds or does; UI labels reuse existing product vocabulary ("discourse context", not an invented synonym — #1255)
- grep the diff for positional child access on settings/config trees (`tree[3]`, `.children[0]`) → look up by key with `getSubTree`; position compiles today and silently writes to the wrong parent after any reorder (#1302)
- persisted/saved data stores stable IDs (shape id, uid), never display names — names are UI-only and subject to change (#1222: save `frameShapeId`, not `frameName`)
- `Page`, `Block`, and `Any` are reserved built-in vocabulary: excluded from user-selectable type lists (#1298), never name-resolved to/from a remote schema, never creatable as configured types (#1331 was blocked on exactly this; #1272 applied the same rule on canvas)
- a panel that replaces or extends existing UI matches it pixel-wise — proportions, selected-tab highlight, centering; reviewers screenshot-compare against the original (#1255, #1272). Empty states key on the right condition (no relation *instances* ≠ no relation *types*, #1255)
- user-facing strings use user vocabulary — a toast saying "backfilled" is a finding; internal bookkeeping reports to PostHog only (#1332)

- Every hunk maps to this PR's ticket; unrelated changes → revert or explicitly annotate. Out-of-scope improvements a reviewer might request → pre-empt by naming them in the PR with a Linear ticket ("X is deferred to ENG-YYYY").
- **One problem, ~<500 lines.** A PR solves a single problem in under ~500 changed lines before tests (mdroidian's stated bar, #1222). Real drive-by bug fixes split into their own ticket — and get fixed at their source layer (a roamjs-components bug is fixed in roamjs-components, not patched locally).
- **Bot-comment gate.** Before requesting human review: every codex/graphite/devin comment is either fixed or answered with why-not, and resolved. mdroidian's first pass is frequently just "See codex comments" / "address the bot reviews … and click resolve" (#1257, #1309, #1320) — an unresolved bot thread costs a full review round-trip.
- **Chain coverage.** For a PR in a stacked or sibling-ticket chain: does the union of this PR + named sibling tickets cover both platforms and both data directions? 173	---
174	name: scope-check
175	description: Compare a pull request or Git diff with a Linear engineering ticket's Done When criteria and produce a copy-ready PR scope check. Use when preparing or reviewing a PR, checking whether an implementation introduced broader abstractions or unsupported cases, or documenting why added scope is required now.

177	
178	# Scope Check
179	
180	Compare the completed change with its acceptance boundary. Return a copy-ready `Scope check` section unless the user requests the analysis too.
181	
182	## Gather the Inputs
183	
184	1. Resolve the Linear issue from an explicit `ENG-###` identifier, then from the PR or branch name. Fetch the issue with the Linear connector. If it is unavailable, ask for the ticket's `Problem`, `Solution`, and `Done When` sections.
185	2. Treat `Done When` as the acceptance boundary. Use `Problem` and `Solution` only to clarify that boundary, not to silently expand it.
186	3. Resolve the final change set from the supplied diff or PR. For a PR, inspect its metadata and complete diff. For the current branch, compare it with the PR base branch and include staged and unstaged changes.
187	4. Read linked decisions or ticket comments only when they explain an apparent scope expansion.
188	
189	## Evaluate Scope
190	
191	Map every material behavior or architectural change to a `Done When` criterion.
192	
193	- Treat implementation details, tests, documentation, and generated files required to satisfy `Done When` as in scope.
194	- Flag broader abstractions, unrelated refactors, new dependencies, migrations, or support for cases not required by `Done When`.
195	- Do not treat a change as in scope only because it is useful or adjacent.
196	
197	For each scope expansion, determine:
198	
199	1. What broader abstraction or additional case was introduced?
200	2. Which current use case or ticket requires it, and why must it be included now rather than deferred?
201	3. Was anyone affected or consulted, and where is the discussion or decision recorded?
202	
203	Do not invent missing justification. Mark it `Not documented` and recommend recording it in a Linear comment before the PR is merged.
204	
205	## Format the Result
206	
207	Use this form when the diff stays within scope:
208	
209	```markdown
210	## Scope check
211	
212	- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
213	- Scope beyond `Done When`: None.
214	```
215	
216	Use this form when the diff expands scope:
217	
218	```markdown
219	## Scope check
220	
221	- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
222	- Scope beyond `Done When`: <what changed>
223	- Required now: <use case or ticket and why it cannot be deferred>
224	- Anyone affected or consulted: <Yes, No, or Not documented>
225	- Decision: <link to the discussion or decision, or `Not documented`>
226	```
227	
228	If the ticket or diff cannot be resolved, leave the checkbox unchecked and state exactly what input is missing. Keep findings short and evidence-based.
229	
230	Do not modify the issue, PR, or implementation unless the user explicitly asks.
231	=================== /home/sid/.claude/commands/pre-pr-review.md
232	---
233	name: pre-pr-review
234	description: Verification-first pre-PR review — mechanical checks against the diff, context docs, and schema, ending with a predicted-review simulation
235	user_invocable: true
236	---
237	
238	<skill-prompt>
239	Run a pre-PR review of the current change set. This is NOT a checklist to ponder — it is a sequence of verification steps with pass/fail outcomes. You must actually run the greps/traces; "I believe this is fine" without having looked is a failed step. Built from an autopsy of 97 real reviewer comments (2026-03→07) — 46 violated rules a previous skill already "had" but never enforced; recall is not verification — and refreshed 2026-08-28 against the 2026-07→08 corpus (~200 human review comments across sid's and teammates' PRs).
240	
241	Required reading before step 1 (both live in `<repo-root>/.claude/context/`, repo root `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph` — reachable by absolute path from any worktree):
242	- `engineering-context.md` — team philosophies and hard-learned lessons (the *why* behind every check below)
243	- `db-domain-invariants.md` — current schema/data-layer facts (the data-layer pass checks the diff against every entry)
244	
245	## Mode gate (run FIRST, before Step 0)
246	
247	Decide which mode this run needs. This is a judgment call you make from evidence — not a rule to apply mechanically, and not something to take on faith from the dispatching prompt (dispatch prompts are written fresh each run and can get this wrong in either direction):
248	- Evidence a full pass already ran on this PR: a previous run's line-anchored annotations posted on the PR, existing review threads answering a prior findings report, or the dispatcher naming a last-reviewed SHA.
249	- Default when a full pass ran and the commits since only answer review feedback: Re-review mode below.
250	- A full pass on a follow-up push can still be the right call when there's genuine reason — the delta added surface beyond the feedback (the escape hatch below), the base moved under the branch, prior coverage looks doubtful or stale, or enough rounds have accumulated that the whole PR deserves fresh eyes. If you judge that, run full and say why.
251	- The first line of your output states the chosen mode and the reasoning — that's what keeps the choice reviewable, whichever way it goes.
252	
253	## Step 0 — Inventory
254	
255	The change set is the FULL PR diff: `git diff <base>...HEAD` (merge-base three-dot against the PR's base branch — the stack parent for stacked PRs, else main) plus staged/unstaged changes. Never review only the latest commits: reviewers see the whole PR, and code that landed on the branch before this run is still your surface. (Exception: Re-review mode below.) Classify changed files:
256	- **DATA**: `packages/database/**`, `*.sql`, any file containing a Supabase/PostgREST call (`.from(`), datalog query, or cross-app contract type
257	- **FRONTEND**: `apps/roam/**`, `apps/obsidian/**`, `apps/website/**` UI code
258	- **OTHER**: tests, docs, config
259	
260	Steps 2 and 3 are scoped: skip the data-layer pass if no DATA files changed; skip the frontend pass if no FRONTEND files changed. Never skip steps 1 and 4.
261	
262	## Re-review mode (follow-up pushes)
263	
264	If a full pre-pr-review already ran on this PR and this run covers a follow-up push (fixes after a review round or a previous run's findings), do NOT repeat the full sequence:
265	
266	- Change set = `git diff <last-reviewed-sha>...HEAD` — the commits since the state the previous round covered, not the whole PR again.
267	- **Findings closure first.** For every finding from the previous run and every reviewer/bot comment since: re-run the SPECIFIC check that produced it and report fixed / not-fixed / deferred+ticket per item. A fix claimed without re-verification is a failed step; a UI fix additionally gets re-driven (existing rule).
268	- Run steps 1–3 mechanically on the delta only, with Step 0's DATA/FRONTEND scoping applied to the delta. Step 4 shrinks to: every new hunk maps to the review feedback or the ticket, and the bot-comment gate on comments the new push attracted.
269	- Skip re-reading the context docs unless the delta touches DATA/FRONTEND files and they aren't already in context.
270	- Escape hatch: if the "follow-up" adds new surface (rebase onto a moved base, new feature code, a refactor beyond what was asked), it is not a re-review — run the full sequence on the full PR diff.
271	
272	## Step 1 — Mechanical sweeps (always run; each is an action, not a question)
273	
274	1a. **Reuse gate.** List every NEW named thing in the diff (function, type, component, constant, enum, marker string). For each, run a grep across `apps/roam/src/utils`, `packages/utils`, `packages/database/src`, and sibling files for the core operation or shape. Report what you searched and what you found. A new thing duplicating an existing one is a finding. Special case: every inline string-literal union (`"X" | "Y"`) gets its members grepped in `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts`; members matching a generated enum → must use `Enums<"…">`.
275	
276	1b. **Justification sweep.** For every added default value, optional prop/field, state variable, fallback (`?? x`, `|| x`), and kept-through-refactor line: name the concrete code path that exercises it. Trace return types through call sites — if a function always returns `T`, a `?? fallback` at its call site is dead code; say so. No path → finding: delete it.
277	
278	1c. **Literal hoist.** Repeated or typo-prone string literals (prop keys, selectors, attribute names, ids) appearing more than once or shared with other files → must be a named constant defined once.
279	
280	1d. **Type honesty.** For every `as`, `any`, `unknown`, `!` (non-null assertion), `?.`, `void`, and `|| default` in the diff: can the value actually be null/absent there? Verify against the type at its source, don't guess. Assertion where a guard or upstream fix is possible → finding. A `!` that must survive gets an inline comment saying why it's safe — mdroidian flags every bare `!` (#1329, #1324).
281	
282	1e. **Explainability.** For each hunk: one sentence, why is this here in service of the ticket? Reorderings, reformats, removals, and leftover scaffolding you can't explain → finding: revert.
283	
284	1f. **Call-graph pass (review the resulting system, not the diff).** For every exported symbol added or modified, and every function parameter added: grep ALL call sites across `apps/` and `packages/` and read them. Findings:
285	- a parameter that only one caller supplies (or that every caller could omit) → internalize or remove it
286	- a wrapper that after this change only renames/forwards or adds one trivial field → collapse it into its caller
287	- an export with zero external consumers → unexport
288	- an existing caller whose behavior silently changes (check what it did with the old return shape — e.g. did it append `Z` to a timestamp you now normalize?)
289	Reviewers read the post-state code, not the diff; a hunk that looks justified in isolation can leave the system with dead indirection.
290	
291	1g. **Comment audit.** List every comment line ADDED by the diff. Delete any that restates the code or narrates the change — "Claude, chill on the comments" is a real review quote, left twice (#1222, #1321), and "some unnecessary comments here" a third time (#1292). A comment referencing context not present in the file (another PR, a discussion, another platform's behavior) either becomes self-contained or dies: reviewers reply "What is F12?" / "What is the same reason?" to comments they can't parse cold (#1315, #1292, #1284). Keep only comments stating a constraint the code can't show.
292	
293	1h. **Second-lookup check.** For every new fetch, map-build, `.find`, or helper lookup: trace where its input data was constructed — was the looked-up value already present there (on the row, the batch, an upstream type)? If yes → thread the field through the pipeline types instead of re-deriving downstream. (#1266: importer re-fetched `schema_id` that `SharedNode` already carried; #1317: `getFormatByNodeTypeUid()` second lookup when `matchingNodeType.format` was in hand at the construction site.)
294	
295	1i. **Workflow injection (only if `.github/workflows/` changed).** Any `${{ inputs.* }}` / `${{ github.event.* }}` interpolated directly into a `run:` script is shell injection — pass it through `env:` and use a quoted variable, validated against a fully anchored pattern (#1253).
296	
297	## Step 2 — Data-layer pass (only if DATA files changed)
298	
299	2a. Open `db-domain-invariants.md` and check the diff against EVERY entry. For each entry state: applies / doesn't apply / VIOLATION. Do not summarize the file — walk it.
300	
301	2b. **Provenance trace.** For every value read from a PostgREST response or datalog result used in the diff: name the source column, grep its type in `packages/database/supabase/schemas/*.sql`, then judge the code handling it (timestamps are the known killer — naive UTC, no `Z`).
302	
303	2c. **Query review.** For every `.from(...)` chain (new or modified): required domain filters present (arity, is_schema, variant)? Any client-side `.filter`/`.find`/sort the request could express? Payload columns in a listing path? Paginated with a unique total order? Inside a loop that should be batched?
304	
305	2d. **Contract check.** New/changed shared types: required-vs-optional modeled from real cases (does every producer actually supply it)? Identity carried once (RID) not duplicated decomposed? Consistent with `crossAppContracts.ts` and with what the Obsidian side already assumes — check its consumer code, don't assume.
306	
307	2e. **Converter matrix.** A field added or renamed on a cross-app contract or schema type must be handled in EVERY converter, BOTH directions, or explicitly deferred with a ticket named in the PR. Enumerate the cells and mark each handled/deferred: `packages/database/src/lib/crossAppConverters.ts` (CrossApp→db), `packages/database/src/lib/dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` (db→CrossApp), `apps/roam/src/utils/roamToCrossAppConverters.ts`, and Obsidian's parse/produce paths (`importNodes.ts` parsers, publish side). maparent asked for the missing direction on #1316 AND #1317: "This PR is adding a field; it should handle that field in both translation directions."
308	
309	2f. **Flag-gated writes.** For every new DB write path: which user-visible flag or action authorizes it? Sync flag off ⇒ the user expects NO DB communication; a silent maintenance write (backfill, migration) needs explicit call-out in the PR, and its outcome reports to PostHog — never a user toast (#1332).
310	
311	## Step 3 — Frontend pass (only if FRONTEND files changed)
312	
313	Check against the frontend lessons in `engineering-context.md`, mechanically:
314	- grep the diff for `style=`, `class-[`/`-[` arbitrary values, hex colors → Tailwind-scale violations
315	- grep for `window.roamAlphaAPI` legacy paths (sync `.q`, `async.backend`) → current-API violations
316	- settings writes → must go through block-props accessors, preserving the store gate
317	- new UI elements → which flag gates them (including EXISTING flags the new surface must respect, e.g. `autoCanvasRelations` on #1272); user-facing failures → PostHog + toast, not `console.error`
318	- names: every new variable/setter/label states exactly what it holds or does; UI labels reuse existing product vocabulary ("discourse context", not an invented synonym — #1255)
319	- grep the diff for positional child access on settings/config trees (`tree[3]`, `.children[0]`) → look up by key with `getSubTree`; position compiles today and silently writes to the wrong parent after any reorder (#1302)
320	- persisted/saved data stores stable IDs (shape id, uid), never display names — names are UI-only and subject to change (#1222: save `frameShapeId`, not `frameName`)
321	- `Page`, `Block`, and `Any` are reserved built-in vocabulary: excluded from user-selectable type lists (#1298), never name-resolved to/from a remote schema, never creatable as configured types (#1331 was blocked on exactly this; #1272 applied the same rule on canvas)
322	- a panel that replaces or extends existing UI matches it pixel-wise — proportions, selected-tab highlight, centering; reviewers screenshot-compare against the original (#1255, #1272). Empty states key on the right condition (no relation *instances* ≠ no relation *types*, #1255)
323	- user-facing strings use user vocabulary — a toast saying "backfilled" is a finding; internal bookkeeping reports to PostHog only (#1332)
324	
325	## Step 4 — Process gate
326	
327	- Every hunk maps to this PR's ticket; unrelated changes → revert or explicitly annotate. Out-of-scope improvements a reviewer might request → pre-empt by naming them in the PR with a Linear ticket ("X is deferred to ENG-YYYY").
328	- **One problem, ~<500 lines.** A PR solves a single problem in under ~500 changed lines before tests (mdroidian's stated bar, #1222). Real drive-by bug fixes split into their own ticket — and get fixed at their source layer (a roamjs-components bug is fixed in roamjs-components, not patched locally).
329	- **Bot-comment gate.** Before requesting human review: every codex/graphite/devin comment is either fixed or answered with why-not, and resolved. mdroidian's first pass is frequently just "See codex comments" / "address the bot reviews … and click resolve" (#1257, #1309, #1320) — an unresolved bot thread costs a full review round-trip.
330	- **Chain coverage.** For a PR in a stacked or sibling-ticket chain: does the union of this PR + named sibling tickets cover both platforms and both data directions? "This only handles Obsidian-origin — where's Roam-origin?" is maparent's most repeated 07–08 comment (#1267, #1269, #1316). Name the gap and the ticket that owns it in the PR before he does.
331	- **Guard removals are argued in the PR.** Removing an existence check or gate: state the cases it protected and why each is now safe (idempotent re-upsert, upstream guarantee). #1280's check removal survived review, but through a 3-comment thread that one PR annotation would have preempted.
332	- **Refactor/extraction parity table.** If this PR moves or extracts code (util → shared package, file split, API swap): produce a table of old symbol → new symbol → `identical` or `changed: <why>`. Every not-1:1 replacement is a decision the reviewer WILL ask about ("could you walk through those decisions?") — enumerate them before they do. The table goes in the PR description.
333	- Runtime proof: does this change have a surface a unit test can't exercise (UI, load-order, multi-user)? If yes, a demo is REQUIRED, not noted (`/demo-handoff`). If the diff touches DOM observers, drag/hover interactions, or rendered Roam surfaces: emit a **regression matrix** — surfaces (main window, right sidebar, left sidebar, Kanban, query-builder link/embed/render views, canvas) × content shapes (single-line, multiline/wrapping, nested references, page titles) — marking which cells this change can affect; the demo must drive every affected cell, with the mouse cursor visible in the recording, and any bug you claim fixed must be re-driven by you after the fix. Video quality bar (#1298): signal each state change visually (a quick caption/toast — "before fix" / "on branch"), don't carry it in narration alone, and cut narration that states the obvious ("every relation has a source and destination" earned a 🙄 from mdroidian).
334	- Reviewer context: list the bullets the PR description must contain (what was removed and why, temporary code, decisions made, deferrals + tickets). Test: could someone review this without asking a question?
335	- **Inherited decisions carry breadcrumbs.** Any code that exists because of a review decision on a PREVIOUS PR (a reviewer's direction, a contract agreed in another thread) gets a draft line-comment citing that source ("per maparent on #1214: local IDs may already be RIDs"). Without the breadcrumb the next reviewer re-litigates it.
336	
337	## Output
338	
339	1. **Findings**, ranked by severity, each: file:line — what — why it matters (cite the context-doc entry or the verification step that failed) — concrete fix.
340	2. **Verification log** — one line per mechanical step: what you ran/checked and the outcome. This proves the steps happened; a review with findings but no log is invalid.
341	2b. **Draft PR annotations** — ready-to-post, line-anchored comments explaining every non-obvious decision (guidepost style: what this block does and why, inherited-decision citations, parity-table deltas). Proven repeatedly: #1214, and in 07–08 reviewers replied to annotations in-thread and accepted the argument (#1280 "I accept this argument. Approving.", #1331). Also annotate every LARGE removal or moved block ("this was refactored into abc.ts") — mdroidian asked for exactly this on #1320. Posting them is part of finishing the PR, not optional polish.
342	2c. All reviewer-facing prose this skill emits — PR description bullets, draft annotations, deferral notes, parity tables — follows the team writing style skill at `<repo-root>/.claude/skills/discourse-engineering-writing-style/SKILL.md` (mdroidian's #1278): lead with the point, one term per concept, replace vague verbs ("handle", "support") with the specific behavior, no em dashes, shortest version that keeps the nuance.
343	3. **Predicted review** (simulation, not identity): given the reviewers' comment history — mdroidian: frontend craftsmanship, dead code, reuse, naming, comment noise, bare `!`, second lookups, design parity with existing UI, reserved vocabulary (Page/Block/Any), unresolved bot comments, demo-video quality, Socratic "why is this here?"; maparent: schema/contract correctness, query shape, the missing converter direction, chain/sibling-ticket coverage gaps ("this only handles Obsidian-origin"), values re-fetched that the pipeline already carries, partial-failure semantics, Obsidian-parity of UX decisions, "worth calling out in another task?", "what does the data look like in 6 months?" — list the comments each would most likely leave on the remaining diff. 344	4. If a pass is clean, say so explicitly. Do not manufacture findings; ~11% of historical review comments were not catchable pre-PR (product/1:1 context) — surface open questions instead of contorting.
345	
346	Anti-weasel rules: no "not harmful, just unnecessary" (unnecessary = delete), no "acceptable for consistency" (a no-op kept for symmetry is cargo-culting), no noting facts without stating the conclusion they imply. If you have the information that leads to a finding, state the finding.

Plan is ready; here it is before I start. Next step is creating the six worktrees off the freshly pulled `main` (`065cab5e`).

## Dependencies
There's no hard dependency, so all six start now in parallel. Three tickets touch shared code, though:

1. **ENG-2195 and ENG-2351** both edit `mapNodeTypeIdToLocal` in `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts`. ENG-2195 owns the `format` derivation in `parseSchemaLiteralContent`. ENG-2351 owns the template block below it. Both can reuse helpers that already exist (`checkInvalidChars`, `sanitizeFileName`, `createTemplateFileWithUniqueName`), so neither needs a new shared helper. Whichever merges second rebases one hunk.
2. **ENG-2348 and your draft #1479 (ENG-2296)** both edit `DiscoverSharedNodesDialog.tsx`, the import entry point. Default: ENG-2348 branches from `main` and adds the warning as a self-contained component rendered by one line, so the rebase stays small. Tell me if you'd rather stack it on `eng-2296`.
3. **ENG-2195 vs ENG-2176:** Michael flagged these as possible duplicates. They aren't. ENG-2195 makes imported formats safe to use as filenames at import time. ENG-2176 makes the format-to-regex builder escape metacharacters in both apps. They don't share any files.

| Ticket | Area | Main entry points |
|---|---|---|
| ENG-2176 | Roam, Obsidian and a shared package (largest; Post v0) | both `getDiscourseNodeFormatExpression` / `extractContentFromTitle` copies, `DiscourseContextView`, `QueryEngine`, `matchDiscourseNode` |
| ENG-2195 | Obsidian | `importNodes.ts`, `validateNodeType.ts` |
| ENG-2348 | Roam | the share dialog and `DiscoverSharedNodesDialog` (a warning, not a block, per the ticket's Solution) |
| ENG-2349 | Roam UI | `TentativeRelationInstances.tsx` (`roam-global-tailwind`) |
| ENG-2350 | Roam | `resolveSharedNodeTypes.ts` and the settings accessors |
| ENG-2351 | Obsidian | `importNodes.ts`, `templates.ts`; first confirm Roam really sends the template without a title |

## Workflow for each ticket
1. **Implementer agent** (Opus, one per worktree):
   - Treats the ticket as the spec and the code as the source of truth, and adds tests.
   - Runs eslint, prettier and tsc, then `pnpm ci:validate` and the app build.
   - Reads the full diff against `STYLE_GUIDE.md`.
   - Commits one worktree at a time behind a lock, with no Co-Authored-By line.
   - Pushes and opens a draft PR from the template, with Loom marked "Pending".
2. **Independent review agent** for each PR runs `/pre-pr-review` (this covers the delegated full-review checkbox), `scope-check` and `dg-pr-adherence-check`. I decide what to act on, the implementer fixes it, and follow-up pushes get re-reviewed. Bot comments get fixed or answered.
3. **Where each one stops:** draft PR open, checks green, review findings closed, Loom pending. Nobody launches Roam. Each PR comes with a live-check runbook for you, and the videos happen in a separate session.

If an agent hits a question the ticket and code don't answer, it picks a default, records it and keeps going. I'll batch those for you. Questions that would change the approach come to you before any code is written.

**Yours to answer:** on ENG-2195, Michael asked why you removed yourself as assignee, and pinged again today. None of the six tickets has an assignee, and I'm not changing that.

# Implementer brief (shared by the six parallel ENG tickets)

You implement one Linear ticket in your own git worktree, end to end, up to an open draft PR. Five other agents are doing the same on sibling tickets in sibling worktrees at the same time. The rules below exist because parallel agents have broken each other before.

## Hard rules

1. **Stay in your worktree.** Every path you edit starts with your worktree path. Never `cd` to `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph` (the main checkout) or into another worktree. Run commands as `(cd <worktree>/apps/<app> && <cmd>)` subshells or with `git -C <worktree>`. Print `pwd` and `git rev-parse --short HEAD` at the top of every check or build command so drift is visible. The main checkout's `.claude/context/*` docs and `.agents/skills/*` files may be READ by absolute path.
2. **Never `git stash`** (refs/stash is shared across all worktrees). Never `git reset --hard`. Never force-push. Never rebase or touch any branch other than yours.
3. **Serialize commits and pushes.** The pre-commit hook (lint-staged) stashes internally, so parallel commits across worktrees race. Always wrap them in the shared lock:
   - `flock /tmp/claude-1000/-mnt-data-projects-discourse-graph/e4326d15-50c9-45c4-b89e-42a575c674d2/scratchpad/git-commit.lock git -C <worktree> commit -F <msgfile>`
   - `flock /tmp/claude-1000/-mnt-data-projects-discourse-graph/e4326d15-50c9-45c4-b89e-42a575c674d2/scratchpad/git-commit.lock git -C <worktree> push -u origin <branch>`
   If lint-staged rewrites files during the commit, re-run your checks on them.
4. **Do not run `pnpm install`.** Dependencies are already installed in your worktree with `--frozen-lockfile`. The only exception: you changed a `package.json` or `pnpm-lock.yaml` (avoid that; both apps already depend on `@repo/utils` and `@repo/database`). If you must install, use `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` at your worktree root and immediately afterwards run `git -C <worktree> config core.hooksPath /mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.husky/_` (husky rewrites it to a relative path, which breaks the shared hooks for everyone). Never use `--no-frozen-lockfile`.
5. **Never launch Roam, Obsidian, a browser, Playwright, or the Roam Local API.** No live-app sessions of any kind. Work is code-only: implement, type-check, test, build. Live verification belongs to sid; you write him a runbook.
6. **No attribution.** No `Co-Authored-By` lines in commits. No "Generated with Claude Code" or any Claude/AI footer in PR bodies or comments.
7. **No Linear writes.** Do not change ticket status, assignee, or labels, and do not comment on Linear. Read-only Linear access (get_issue, list_comments, extract_images) is fine; load those tools via ToolSearch if you need them.
8. **The ticket is the spec; the code is the source of truth.** Do not open the Roam pages or Zoom recordings linked in ticket Notes. When neither the ticket nor the code settles a question:
   - **Blocking** (two plausible implementations with materially different scope, UX, or data shape): stop BEFORE writing code and return the question, your evidence, and a proposed default. You will be resumed with an answer.
   - **Non-blocking**: choose the most conservative default, record it, keep going, and list it in your final report.

## Read before writing code

- Root `AGENTS.md`, `STYLE_GUIDE.md`, `PR_GUIDELINES.md`, `.github/pull_request_template.md` (in your worktree).
- The nested `AGENTS.md` for every app you touch (`apps/roam/AGENTS.md`, `apps/obsidian/AGENTS.md`).
- `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.claude/context/engineering-context.md` (team lessons; the why behind review comments).
- If you touch DATA (`packages/database/**`, a `.from(` query, a cross-app contract type or converter): also `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.claude/context/db-domain-invariants.md`.
- If you touch Roam UI styling: `<worktree>/.agents/skills/roam-global-tailwind/SKILL.md` and follow it.
- For all reviewer-facing prose (PR body, commit messages): `<worktree>/.agents/skills/dg-engineering-writing-style/SKILL.md` (lead with the point, one term per concept, specific verbs, no em dashes).
- For Roam APIs: `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.claude/context/roam-api-surface.md`. Prefer `window.roamAlphaAPI` > roamjs-components > hand-rolled.

## How to implement (what reviewers on this team flag)

- Smallest diff that satisfies `Done When`. No opportunistic cleanups, renames, reorderings, or refactors of code you did not need to change. One problem per PR.
- Reuse before writing: grep `apps/<app>/src/utils`, `packages/utils/src`, `packages/database/src`, and sibling files for an existing helper before adding one. A new helper duplicating an existing one is a review finding.
- No dead code: every added default, optional field, fallback (`??`, `||`), and state variable must have a concrete code path that exercises it. Trace return types; a `?? x` on a value that is never nullish is dead.
- Type honesty: no `as`/`any`/`!` where a guard or upstream fix works. A `!` that must stay gets a comment saying why it is safe.
- Comments: do not add comments that restate code or narrate the change. Only add a comment for a constraint the code cannot show, and make it self-contained (no references to PRs, tickets, or conversations).
- Literals used more than once become a named constant defined once.
- Don't re-fetch a value the pipeline already carries; thread the field through instead.
- User-facing failures: toast + PostHog where the codebase already does that, not `console.error`. User-facing strings use product vocabulary.
- Roam reserved vocabulary: `Page`, `Block`, `Any` are built-in, never treated as configurable node types.
- Tests: add vitest unit tests for the logic you change (`apps/roam` and `apps/obsidian` both run vitest via `pnpm test:unit`; packages may too). Test the behavior in `Done When`, including the unchanged-behavior cases.

## Checks (all must pass before you push)

From the app directory inside your worktree (repeat per app you touched):
1. `npx eslint --max-warnings 0 <changed files>`
2. `npx prettier --check <changed files>`
3. `npx tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck`
4. `pnpm test:unit`

Then from your worktree root:
5. `pnpm ci:validate` (turbo check-types + test:unit). A baseline run of this on the base commit is at `/tmp/claude-1000/-mnt-data-projects-discourse-graph/e4326d15-50c9-45c4-b89e-42a575c674d2/scratchpad/baseline-ci-validate.log` once it finishes; if something fails there too it is pre-existing, so say so rather than fixing it.
6. Build each touched app: `npx turbo run build --filter=roam` and/or `npx turbo run build --filter=@discourse-graphs/obsidian`. (A Roam build without `apps/roam/.env` logs "Not using the database"; that is expected here.)

Then read your complete final diff (`git -C <worktree> diff origin/main...HEAD` plus anything uncommitted) against `STYLE_GUIDE.md` line by line, including every comment you added. Fix what you find.

Size guidance: about 200 changed lines is the target and 400 the soft limit, excluding tests. Above 400, the PR body's Reviewer brief must say why it cannot reasonably be split, plus the main review entry points and testing path.

## Commit, push, open the draft PR

- First commit message: exactly `ENG-#### <exact Linear ticket title>`. Any follow-up commits: one short imperative sentence describing the change. No body boilerplate, no attribution.
- Push your branch (already named with Linear's `gitBranchName`; do not rename it) with the lock above.
- Open a **draft** PR: `gh pr create --draft --base main --head <branch> --title "ENG-#### <exact Linear ticket title>" --body-file <file>`. If `gh pr edit` is ever needed later, it fails on this repo (classic Projects GraphQL); use `gh api -X PATCH repos/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pulls/<n> -F body=@<file>` instead.
- PR body: start from `.github/pull_request_template.md` and keep its headings.
  - `## Reviewer brief`: only the fields that help (Result, Review focus, Risk or follow-up). Decisions you made where the ticket was silent go under Review focus. "Not yet exercised in Roam/Obsidian" goes under Risk. Do not restate the ticket, no file-by-file summary, no implementation diary.
  - `## Verification`: the commands you ran and their results, on the SHA you pushed.
  - `## Loom video`: `Pending.`
  - `## Scope check`, `## Standards check`, `## Local delegated full review`: keep the template checkboxes UNCHECKED. An independent reviewer runs those; the orchestrator fills them in.
  - Remove the template's HTML comments and any section that is empty and optional.

## Final report (your last message; the orchestrator reads it, sid does not)

1. PR URL, branch, pushed head SHA.
2. Changed files with added/removed line counts, separating tests from non-tests.
3. Check results (each of the six checks above, pass/fail, with the failing output if any).
4. Decisions you made where the ticket and code were silent: the question, what you chose, and why.
5. Open questions for sid, each with a proposed default.
6. A live-check runbook for sid: numbered steps in Roam and/or Obsidian that prove each `Done When` item, including setup (what graph/vault state, which setting), what to click, and what he should see.
7. Anything you deferred, and why.
Keep it tight and factual. Do not claim anything you did not run.

input.prompt:
You are the implementer for Linear ticket ENG-2176 in the discourse-graph monorepo.

- Worktree: /mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/eng-2176
- Branch (already checked out, from origin/main 065cab5e): eng-2176-escape-regex-metacharacters-in-discourse-node-format
- PR title: `ENG-2176 Escape regex metacharacters in discourse node format expressions`

FIRST read the shared brief and follow it exactly: /tmp/claude-1000/-mnt-data-projects-discourse-graph/e4326d15-50c9-45c4-b89e-42a575c674d2/scratchpad/implementer-brief.md

## The ticket (verbatim; this is the spec)

### Problem
* `getDiscourseNodeFormatExpression` (same logic in `apps/obsidian/src/utils/getDiscourseNodeFormatExpression.ts` and `apps/roam/src/utils/getDiscourseNodeFormatExpression.ts`) escapes only `[ ] ? . +` before substituting `{placeholder}` with `(.*?)`. A format containing any other metacharacter — `( ) * ^ $ |` — builds a regex that never matches its own titles: `Claim (draft) - {content}` compiles to `^Claim (draft) - (.*?)$`, which requires the literal title `Claim draft …` and turns `(draft)` into a capture group. Source: Codex P2 on #1318 (https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1318#discussion_r3815409797).
* Consequences by call site:
  * Obsidian `extractContentFromTitle` (ENG-2154/#1318): no match → `core_title` falls back to the full decorated basename — a non-null wrong value that null-probe backfills (ENG-2155-style) skip.
  * A literal `(…)` group also breaks the placeholder↔capture-group 1:1 invariant that the positional `{content}` lookups in both #1318 and #1317 rely on — though misextraction needs the mangled regex to still match a real title (an alternation or an aligned stray group), so the dominant failure in practice is the no-match fallback above.
  * Obsidian QueryEngine (×2), `createNode`, `DiscourseContextView`, and Roam `matchDiscourseNode`: metachar formats silently never match, so those nodes are invisible to format matching.

### Solution
* Escape every regex metacharacter in the literal portions of the format while leaving `{[a-zA-Z]+}` placeholders intact (substitute placeholders first or split on them, then escape the literal segments — a blanket escape would also escape the braces and break substitution).
* Fix both apps in one PR: the builders must stay identical or `core_title` semantics diverge cross-app.
* Preferred shape: hoist `getDiscourseNodeFormatExpression` + `extractContentFromTitle` into a shared package (pure cross-app text transforms belong there, and a package has a vitest runner that apps/obsidian lacks), replacing the per-app copies, the divergent inline copy in `DiscourseContextView.tsx` (which can render a different Content string than the published `core_title`), and Roam's wider `{[\w\d-]+}` placeholder scan (#1317) that mismatches its builder. One grammar, one implementation, tested. Per-app grammar constants are the fallback if the hoist is blocked.

### Done When
* `Claim (draft) - {content}` matches its titles and extracts `content` in both apps.
* One shared, unit-tested implementation of builder + extractor (at minimum: scan and builder share one grammar constant per app), and `DiscourseContextView` renders the same content string the converter publishes.
* Formats without metacharacters behave identically to today.

### Out of Scope
* Value-aware repair of `core_title` rows already written with the fallback value (same follow-up story as ENG-2155's wrong-value pass).

### Notes
* Deferred from #1318 because the builder has five Obsidian call sites plus the Roam matchers — matching behavior changes everywhere, so it needs its own PR and test pass.

Ticket comments: Michael Gartner flagged ENG-2195 ("Normalize imported node type formats for Obsidian filenames") as a possible duplicate. It is not: ENG-2195 normalizes imported formats for filename safety at the Obsidian schema-import boundary and is being implemented by a sibling agent right now. Do not touch `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts`'s `parseSchemaLiteralContent`/`mapNodeTypeIdToLocal` or `validateNodeType.ts` unless a builder call site there forces it.

## Orchestrator recon (facts to save you time; verify, don't trust blindly)

- Files referencing `getDiscourseNodeFormatExpression` or `extractContentFromTitle` on main:
  - Obsidian: `src/utils/conceptConversion.ts`, `src/components/DiscourseContextView.tsx`, `src/services/QueryEngine.ts`, `src/utils/extractContentFromTitle.ts`, `src/utils/createNode.ts`, `src/utils/getDiscourseNodeFormatExpression.ts`
  - Roam: `src/components/CreateRelationDialog.tsx`, `src/components/settings/DiscourseNodeSpecification.tsx`, `src/utils/roamToCrossAppConverters.ts`, `src/utils/discourseNodeSearch.ts`, `src/utils/discourseNodeSearchProviders.ts`, `src/utils/syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts`, `src/utils/discourseNodeFormatToDatalog.ts`, `src/utils/matchDiscourseNode.ts`, `src/utils/extractContentFromTitle.ts`, `src/utils/getDiscourseNodeFormatExpression.ts`, `src/utils/conceptConversion.ts`, `src/utils/sourceSlot.ts`, `src/utils/getAllDiscourseNodesSince.ts`, plus tests `src/utils/__tests__/{extractContentFromTitle,sourceSlot,materializeSharedNode}.test.ts`
  - Shared: `packages/database/src/lib/decorateTitle.ts` (the shared title decorator both apps already use).
- Both apps already depend on `@repo/utils` (`packages/utils/src` has `resolveSchemaFormat.ts`, `execContext.ts`, ...) and `@repo/database`. Hoisting needs no new dependency, so no `pnpm install`. Pick the package with evidence (where the related decorate logic and format helpers already live), and say why in the PR.
- Obsidian now has a vitest runner (`apps/obsidian` `pnpm test:unit`); the ticket's "apps/obsidian lacks" remark is stale, but the hoist is still the ticket's preferred shape.
- `apps/roam/src/utils/sourceSlot.ts` is a self-described temporary v0 hack for the Roam-only `{Source}` fill, slated for removal by ENG-2043/DES-368. Keep it working through the change, but do not widen the shared helper's API just for it; adapt sourceSlot locally if it calls a function you replace.
- Datalog: `discourseNodeFormatToDatalog.ts` builds Roam query clauses from the format. Check whether it builds a regex string for datalog `re-pattern`; if so, the escape must be right for that consumer too, and say so in the PR.
- Unifying Roam's `{[\w\d-]+}` scan with the `{[a-zA-Z]+}` builder grammar can change which placeholders Roam recognizes (digits, `_`, `-`). Check real format usage in the code (default formats, tests, settings) before choosing; if the choice changes behavior for any plausible existing format, record it as a decision for sid.

## Extra PR requirements for this ticket

- This is an extraction across packages, so the PR body's Reviewer brief must include a parity table: old symbol → new symbol → `identical` or `changed: <why>` for every replaced copy (both app builders, both extractors, the DiscourseContextView inline copy, Roam's placeholder scan).
- If the non-test diff exceeds 400 changed lines, include the split justification (the ticket requires one PR for both apps) plus review entry points and testing path.
- Tests must cover: `Claim (draft) - {content}` and other metacharacters `( ) * ^ $ | . + ? [ ]` in literal segments; formats with multiple placeholders; formats with no metacharacters (unchanged results); the DiscourseContextView path rendering the same string as the converter.

Finish with the final report described in the brief.

input.prompt:
You are the implementer for Linear ticket ENG-2195 in the discourse-graph monorepo.

- Branch (already checked out, from origin/main 065cab5e): eng-2195-normalize-imported-node-type-formats-for-obsidian-filenames

FIRST read the shared brief and follow it exactly: /tmp/claude-1000/-mnt-data-projects-discourse-graph/e4326d15-50c9-45c4-b89e-42a575c674d2/scratchpad/implementer-brief.md

## The ticket (verbatim; this is the spec)

### Problem
* Imported schemas can persist Roam formats such as `[[CLM]] - {content}` without Obsidian's filename validation.
* When no matching local type exists, title decoration can create files such as `[[CLM]] - sleep improves memory.md`.
* ENG-2157 ("Decorate imported node titles in Obsidian from `core_title`") now relies on the local type's format, so imported formats need the same filename safety as locally created types.

### Solution
* Normalize incoming node type formats before storing them locally, then apply the same invalid filename character checks used by Obsidian titles and node type formats.
* Store `[[CLM]] - {content}` as `CLM - {content}`, while preserving `{content}` and other valid formatting.
* Leave an existing matching local type and its format unchanged.

### Done When
* A type created from `[[CLM]] - {content}` stores `CLM - {content}` and decorates an imported file as `CLM - sleep improves memory.md`.
* Incoming formats containing `#`, `^`, `[`, `]`, or `|` cannot be persisted without normalization, and the result passes the existing format validation.
* Unit tests cover bracketed formats, other invalid filename characters, and valid formats remaining unchanged. This is limited to the schema import boundary.

### Out of Scope
* Rewriting formats already stored on local node types or changing the source schema.
* Changes to the title decoration behavior delivered in ENG-2157.
* Broader node format validation or format migration.

### Notes
* Follow-up to ENG-2157 and PR #1330.
* Relevant paths: `parseSchemaLiteralContent` / `mapNodeTypeIdToLocal` in `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts`, and `checkInvalidChars` / `validateNodeFormat` in `apps/obsidian/src/utils/validateNodeType.ts`.

Ticket comments: Michael asked sid about the assignee (ignore; that is sid's to answer) and flagged ENG-2176 ("Escape regex metacharacters in discourse node format expressions") as a possible duplicate. It is not: ENG-2176 fixes the format→regex builder in both apps and is being implemented by a sibling agent right now. ENG-2348 (#1506) is getting a short render test. Everything else keeps running, but ENG-2195 (#1507) needs two decisions from you.

**ENG-2195 Done When 2 says "the result passes the existing format validation".** The PR only satisfies the invalid-character part of it. Running the real code showed two gaps:
- `[[CLM]] - {Content}` becomes `CLM - {Content}`, which fails Obsidian's case-sensitive `{content}` rule.
- `[[HYP]] - {content}` becomes `HYP - {content}`. If a local type with a different name already uses that format, the two collide.

The collision is new harm from this PR. Obsidian checks uniqueness on every settings save (`NodeTypeSettings.tsx:770`), so it would refuse to save any edit to the user's own local type. The imported type is read-only, so the user can't fix it from that side. Roam's `[[CLM]]` and `[[QUE]]` defaults normalize to exactly Obsidian's defaults, so this happens whenever the type names differ.

- **Option B (my recommendation):** at import, if the normalized format still fails `validateNodeFormat` against the vault's types, fall back to the name-derived default (normalized). Canonicalize `{Content}` to `{content}` first. If the default also collides, store it anyway and document that. This is about 20–30 lines in a small pure helper with tests.
- **Option A:** keep the character rule only. The PR body documents the collision and cites ENG-2346 for the `{content}` rule.

**`specImport.ts` (importing schema files) also stores formats without normalizing them.** It's only exposed through types imported before this PR, which the ticket puts out of scope for rewriting.
- **Recommended:** defer it with a follow-up ticket, and fix the PR body's wrong reason for skipping it.
- **Alternative:** include it now, about 4 lines.

Whichever you pick, the implementer also gets the reviewer's other fixes: normalize the name-derived default, reword a comment, fix one test title, and update the PR body.

> Not a duplicate of ENG-2176. ENG-2176 escapes regex metacharacters when a format becomes a match expression. ENG-2195 removes `#`, `^`, `[`, `]` and `|` from imported formats before they're stored. They overlap only on `^` and `|`, and escaping alone doesn't fix `|`: `sanitizeFileName` drops it from file names, so an escaped `\|` still doesn't match.
